takeaway: The four normal oesophageal constrictions: cricopharyngeus (15 cm), aortic arch (22.5 cm), left main bronchus (27.5 cm), lower oesophageal sphincter (40 cm). The left atrium indents it only when dilated.

lines.text: The normal oesophagus has four constrictions, seen on video fluoroscopy.
The first, and narrowest, is the cricopharyngeus muscle, fifteen centimetres from the incisors.
The second is the aortic arch, at twenty-two and a half centimetres.
Then the left main bronchus, at twenty-seven and a half.
And the lower oesophageal sphincter, at forty centimetres.
But the left atrium does not indent the normal oesophagus.
lines.say: (clears throat) But the left atrium does not indent the normal oesophagus.

lines.text: It does so only when it is enlarged, in left atrial dilatation.
So the answer is the left atrium.
